thread:
Olivia: FYI AcmeBank security reviewer asked for a concise KMS/key access proof pack (diagram + subprocessor mapping + short attestation). Need this to attach to their SIG questionnaire.
Mike: Got it. Do they want both Redwood-managed keys and BYOK flows documented? That's the usual ask.
Olivia: Yes — they want both options and explicit answers on whether any subprocessor could see unwrapped keys or plaintext at any point.
Rachel: Quick summary: with Redwood-managed keys we use envelope encryption; data keys are generated per-blob, stored encrypted, and only decrypted in RAM on runtime workers. No human or external vendor gets unwrapped key material. With BYOK, customer KMS holds the master key; Redwood never stores the unwrapped master key.
Tom: Ops note: runtime uses ephemeral VMs in region (us-east-1 / eu-west-1). KMS Decrypts are performed by service account `redwood-runtime@prod` and are visible in KMS audit logs. Persistent stores (object store, backups) contain only encrypted blobs. We can provide a redacted audit line.
Mike: Customer also wants to see which subprocessors touch which hop (e.g., KMS, storage, monitoring). Legal wants exact scope strings for the vendor risk team.
Rachel: Proposed subprocessor table (we'll produce CSV):
- CloudProviderX — KMS + compute, KMS audit only, hypervisor admin: no plaintext access; evidence: KMS audit export link.
- StorageVendorY — encrypted object storage, no key material; evidence: storage encryption cert + DPA excerpt.
- ObservabilityCo — metrics and aggregates only; evidence: SOC2 summary.
Olivia: Can we also include a one-line attestation for the SIG response? Something short legal can sign.
Rachel: Draft attestation: "Redwood Inference attests that when using Redwood-managed keys, unwrapped data keys exist only in ephemeral memory on runtime nodes and are never persisted. Access to key material is restricted to the service principal `redwood-runtime@prod`. No listed subprocessors have access to unwrapped key material. Under BYOK, the customer-managed master key is not disclosed to Redwood; Redwood receives only wrapped data keys."
Tom: I'll export a minimal dataflow PNG and a CSV mapping subprocessor->scope->evidence and drop into the internal POC folder.
Mike: Please include a redacted KMS audit sample (one-line JSON) showing principal, key_id, action=Decrypt, result=OK — that usually resolves compliance questions.
Rachel: Will redact timestamps and any identifying request IDs. Also adding a short snippet of runtime config for proof:
```
service_account: redwood-runtime@prod
kms_key_id: projects/prod/locations/global/keyRings/llm/cryptoKeys/rlw
operation: kms.keys.decrypt
```
Olivia: Timeline: AcmeBank wants the pack by EOD Thursday. Can we have drafts by tomorrow afternoon for legal review?
Tom: Yes — I'll upload draft assets to https://redwood-internal/pocts/acmebank/kms-pack (internal). Files: dataflow.png, subproc_scope.csv, kms_audit_redacted.txt
Rachel: I'll finalize attestation text for SIG/CAIQ and prep BYOK language. Also include a short bullet list of mitigations (token scrubbing, backup encryption, key rotation).
Mike: I'll review sales-facing wording and confirm nothing is overpromising. Olivia: please ping when uploaded.
sec-bot: Reminder set for 2024-03-14 15:00 UTC to check deliverable status :alarm_clock:
Olivia: Thanks team — once uploaded I'll send to AcmeBank security.
